Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Marcus Hale, CFO; Jordan Lee, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Lena Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 marked a period of significant advancement for Voltara Motors, as we continued to execute our strategic plan. Key achievements included record production ramps at our Spartanburg Gigafactory, strong delivery growth for the Voltara Apex sedan capturing meaningful U.S. market share, meaningful gross margin expansion from cost efficiencies and favorable mix, resilient supply chain performance despite headwinds, OTA software rollouts enhancing vehicle capabilities, expansion of our order backlog reflecting sustained demand, and targeted pricing actions driving volume while preserving profitability. The launch of our Voltara Apex has been incredibly successful, and we are seeing a very positive impact on our brand image with rising market share in the midsize EV segment.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. For Q3, our revenue was $2.3 billion, representing a substantial 52% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin reached 19.2%, driven by increased production efficiencies, favorable product mix with higher premium trim adoption, and material cost deflation particularly in batteries. Operating expenses totaled $485 million, reflecting investments in R&D and scaling operations, and net income amounted to $142 million. We are in a strong financial position with $2.8 billion in cash reserves and $1.8 billion undrawn credit facilities. We project revenue of $2.7 to $2.9 billion for Q4, with continued margin expansion.

Let me expand on some key financial aspects. First, on gross margins, we delivered automotive gross margins of 19.2% on a GAAP basis in Q3, up 240 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 510 basis points year-over-year. This stemmed from our Spartanburg Gigafactory ramping to 92% capacity utilization on the Apex sedan lines, a richer mix with 62% of deliveries from high-margin Voltara Horizon SUV and Apex variants, and a 14% sequential drop in LFP battery cell costs to $90 per kWh via long-term deals with CATL and our Reno joint venture ramp.

Looking ahead, for Q4 we guide consolidated gross margins to 20% to 21%, with automotive at 20.5% to 21.5%. Full-year 2024 guidance is now 18.5% to 19%, up 380 basis points from 2023. This assumes 28,000 to 31,000 vehicle deliveries, with global weighted average ASPs stable at $49,200, reflecting 42% premium trims like Horizon Max and Apex Plus.

Key drivers include volume leverage from Q4 production of 29,000 to 32,000 units across Spartanburg, Leipzig, and Shanghai facilities—25% sequential growth at midpoint, dropping depreciation per vehicle to $1,700. Material costs see battery packs at $85 to $90 per kWh, with lithium at $13,500 per ton and 4680 cells at 28% mix via our Nevada output at 22 GWh run-rate, cutting $5 per kWh. Pricing holds with U.S. at $53,000 aided by $7,500 IRA rebates at 88% take-rate, Europe at $48,500 with incentives, China at $33,000 but offset by $280 million regulatory credits.

Regionally, U.S. (58% volume) targets 23% margins, Europe (24%) 17.5%, China (18%) 13.5% improving on localization. Our Margin 26 initiative eyes 26% by 2026 via localization capex, skateboard platforms with gigacasting, and 90% margin software subs at $199 monthly.

On gross margin per vehicle, Q3 hit $14,100 or 27.1% of $52,000 ASP—up $1,400 or 11% YoY from $12,700, and $500 sequentially. Mix was 55% premium Horizon SUV at $65,000 ASP, with $4,500 average U.S. credits. COR per vehicle dropped 13% to $37,900, led by $58/kWh cells (27% YoY down), 23% lower body costs at $4,100 via unboxed process and 99% automation, freight at $1,050. U.S.: $15,800 or 30%; Europe: $12,200 or 24.5%; China: $9,800 or 20.5%. Q4 guide: $14,500-$14,900.

Turning to delivery volume guidance: Q3 saw 26,500 units, up 30% YoY. Q4: 28,000-31,000 total.

- Apex Sedan ($39k-$46k): 11,500-13,000 (42% mix), up on Shanghai Phase 2 for cylindrical cells, 65% U.S. with IRA.
- Horizon SUV ($56k-$71k): 13,000-14,500 (47%), Fremont structural packs, NA fleet deals.
- Pulse Pickup ($76k-$96k): 3,500-4,500 (11%), Texas ramp with V2G.

FY2025: 450,000-500,000; NA 60%, China/APAC 25%, Europe 15%.

On pricing strategies and promotions: Q3 ASP $49,200, down 6% YoY but flat QoQ via Aurora engine. Incentives $1.3B or 5% revenue, like 1.8% APR driving 24% retail surge. U.S. ASP $53k with IRA; Europe €53k with rebates; China RMB190k with 0% down. Leases 30%, residuals 59%. This added $3B EBITDA lift, Q4 ASP $48,500-$50,000.

Finally, order backlog: $29.5B or 192,000 units, +14% QoQ, +25% YoY. Reservations 465,000, +20% QoQ. Apex 60% ($17.7B), Horizon 29% ($8.6B), Pulse 11% ($3.2B). Net adds 45,000, cancellations 4%. NA 72%, Europe 18%, APAC 10%. Q4 to $33-36B.

Next, Jordan Lee will share updates on manufacturing.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Marcus. We have made significant investments in our manufacturing facilities to enhance capacity and improve efficiency. Our Spartanburg Gigafactory reached 18,000 units per month, Leipzig added 5,000 capacity, and Shanghai JV hit 98% utilization. The unboxed process and gigacasting yielded 22% labor savings, with Q3 production at 27,000 units—record volumes—and 15% lower costs per vehicle through dry electrode lines boosting density to 275 Wh/kg. We're on track for 300,000 annual capacity in Spartanburg by mid-2025 and a new Mexico plant.

After me, we'll hear from Dr. Lena Kim on technological advancements.

Dr. Lena Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. Our R&D team continues to push the boundaries of innovation in battery technology, autonomous driving, and connectivity. OTA 3.2 rolled to 82% fleet, enabling 350kW charging and Level 3 ADAS on 2.6B miles data. Solid-state at TRL-6 promises 500 Wh/kg, in-house powertrain at 72% content, and V2G for Pulse unlocking utilities. We're shaping mobility's future.

Following me, Sarah Chen will provide insights into supply chain.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Kim. We've implemented robust strategies to mitigate risks and ensure material flow. In Q3, constraints impacted 10% production, down from 20% prior, from 22% semiconductor shortfalls for inverters (shorting 15,000 units, $380M revenue hit) and lithium up 15% to $27,500/ton idling 12% lines. Nickel up 28%. U.S. port delays added 12 days, Europe CBAM +6% costs, Red Sea +40% freight; Shanghai at 97% on-time.

Trends: Chips surplus by Q4 per Gartner, lithium stabilizing with Brazil projects, cobalt tight. Mitigations: Dual-source chips (Renesas/NXP, 1.3M units, 96% fill); Tier 1 battery mix (Panasonic 38%, etc.), leads to 42 days. Nevada gigafactory at 22 GWh for LFP/NMC, Redwood recycling 94% black mass saving 20%. AI Control Tower 93% disruption accuracy, air-freighted key parts recovering $90M. Hedged 72% lithium, inventory 45 days. Offtakes with Albemarle 110ktpa, QuantumScape pilots. Q4 production unimpacted, enabling 32% growth.

Thank you. Elena, over to you for strategic outlook before Q&A.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, for that comprehensive update on our Q3 results. Before we open the line for questions, I'd like to share our strategic outlook and key priorities for Q4 2024 and fiscal 2025. As we navigate a dynamic EV landscape with demand growth moderating from 35% YoY in 2023 to 25% in 2024 per BloombergNEF, Voltara is focused on execution, innovation, and margin expansion for sustainable profitability.

For Q4, our goal is 28,000 deliveries, +15% QoQ from 24,300 in Q3—on track for 2025 guidance of 140,000-160,000, led by Apex at 12% U.S. midsize share ahead of Hyundai Ioniq 6. U.S. (65%): IRA $7,500 on 85%, Spartanburg to 18,000/month, 22% margins via AESC LFP cutting COGS 8%. Europe (25%): Horizon for CO2 targets, Leipzig +5,000 capacity, 7,000 deliveries despite German subsidy cuts, EU battery passports vs. tariffs. China/APAC (10%): CATL JV for 4680 at 20% cost parity.

OTA 3.2 to 80% fleet: 350kW charging, Level 3 neural nets on 2.5B miles. Q4 capex $450M on dry electrode to 280 Wh/kg.

For FY2025, revenue $8.2-9.0B (+45-60%), EBITDA $250-400M positive, margins 24-26% on 70% in-house powertrain.

Priorities: 1. Portfolio: Pulse crossover Q2'25 at $38k/400-mile NMC, targeting Mach-E segment; Apex Plus V2G H2. 2. Scale: Spartanburg 300k/year, $1.2B Mexico. 3. Batteries/chain: Solid-state TRL-7 with Argonne, 500 Wh/kg; nickel 50/50 Australia-Indonesia. 4. Software: Recurring to 8% via $199/month subs, VPP. 5. Sustainability: 95% recycled per EU regs.

Risks: Lithium $12k/ton, policy shifts; buffered by $2.5B liquidity. We're building the EV ecosystem.

Operator, we're now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to register a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Johnson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Can you elaborate on Q4 delivery guidance by model and regional assumptions?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Mike. As Marcus detailed, Q4 is 28,000-31,000 total, with Apex sedan 11,500-13,000 leveraging Shanghai optimizations for IRA-qualified U.S. demand; Horizon SUV 13,000-14,500 on Fremont structural packs and fleets; Pulse pickup 3,500-4,500 from Texas with V2G edge. NA 65%, Europe 25% navigating subsidies, China 10% on localization—conservative amid macros but conviction on ramps.

Operator:
Our next question from Lisa Chen, Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
Great, thanks. On gross margin guidance, what are the key assumptions and risks?

Marcus Hale:
Lisa, Q4 20.5-21.5% automotive assumes 29k-32k production, $85-90/kWh packs with stable lithium $13.5k, 28% 4680 mix, flat ASP $49.2k. Tailwinds: 150bps fixed leverage, 90bps materials, 70bps mix/credits. Risks: Freight from Red Sea, competition, IRA audits—but upside from credits >$300M. Positions for FY25 24-26%.

Operator:
Next from David Patel, JPMorgan.

David Patel:
Thanks. Jordan or Sarah, update on manufacturing constraints and supply mitigations?

Jordan Lee:
David, Sarah covered supply well—10% Q3 impact down sharply. We've mitigated via diversification: chips <25% any vendor, batteries four Tier 1s at 42-day leads; Nevada 22 GWh recycling via Redwood; AI tower 93% accurate. Spartanburg efficiencies add resilience, targeting zero constraints Q4 for 300k capacity path.

Operator:
From Emma Rodriguez, Barclays.

Emma Rodriguez:
Thanks. Dr. Kim, thoughts on tech roadmap tying to margins?

Dr. Lena Kim:
Emma, OTA 3.2 boosts value, subs at $199/month for 90% margins adding 200bps FY25. Solid-state TRL-7 for 500 Wh/kg/1,000 cycles, 72% powertrain integration, V2G partnerships—recurring to 8% revenue, key for profitability.

Operator:
From Tom Reilly, Citi.

Tom Reilly:
Appreciate it. Sarah, more on supply chain trends and long-term resilience?

Sarah Chen:
Tom, semis recover to surplus Q4, lithium stabilizes with Brazil 270ktpa, but cobalt tight. Strategies: Albemarle offtake $18k floor, QuantumScape pilots, 45-day inventory vs. peers' lower. Unlike GM/Ford idles, our buffer and localization cap 4% net impact, set for 35% 2025 growth.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Operator:
Our final question from Karen Wong, Deutsche Bank.

Karen Wong:
Thanks. Elena, on backlog trends and pricing impact?

Elena Vasquez:
Karen, backlog $29.5B/192k up 14% QoQ, reservations 465k +20%, 42% conversion. Pricing dynamic via engine held ASP, promos 5% revenue drove velocity—$48.2k Q3, stabilizing Q4 with subs adding $150 equiv. Cancellations 4% macro-driven but refundables help; signals 450k-500k FY25.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for electric vehicles and deliver strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
